record.paper_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
record.original_question: Given a particular exact solution u0(x, t) of an integrable system, can the action of infinitely many symmetries introduce an infinite sequence of arbitrary constants into that solution, extending the familiar fact that spatial and temporal translation symmetries can introduce finitely many constants such as x0 and t0 into u0(x − x0, t − t0)?

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 5: Arbitrary constants in special solutions via symmetry transformations
It is a well-established principle that for a particular solution of a given system, denoted as u0(x, t), the incorporation of an arbitrary constant is feasible through the application of a symmetry. Specifically, by invoking the invariance under spatial translation in the x-direction and temporal translation in the t-direction, it is possible to seamlessly integrate two arbitrary constants, represented as {x0, t0}. ... The question that arises is whether the leverage of an infinitely many symmetries could permit the introduction of an infinite series of arbitrary constants into a specific solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an integrable evolution equation be given, possessing infinitely many commuting Lie-point or generalized symmetries, and let u_0(x,t) be a particular exact solution. It is classical that the spatial-translation symmetry ∂_x and temporal-translation symmetry ∂_t allow one to embed two arbitrary constants x_0, t_0 into the solution, producing the family u_0(x − x_0, t − t_0). More generally, applying the flow exp(εK) of any symmetry K admitted by the equation to u_0 yields a one-parameter family of exact solutions depending on the arbitrary constant ε.

Question: Does there exist a particular exact solution u_0(x,t) of an integrable system such that the action of its infinite hierarchy of (commuting) symmetries can be used to introduce an infinite sequence of independent arbitrary constants {c_1, c_2, c_3, …} into u_0, yielding an exact solution that genuinely depends on infinitely many independent parameters? Equivalently, can the infinite-dimensional symmetry algebra of an integrable system act effectively (with infinitely many independent orbit directions) on at least one explicit solution, so that infinitely many essential constants are introduced through symmetry transformations alone?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on infinitely many symmetries of integrable systems (2024, also published in Mathematics MDPI 2024). The survey discusses progress and a related conjecture that all known infinitely many symmetries reduce to linear combinations of finite wave-parameter translation symmetries, but no resolution of the question concerning the introduction of infinitely many arbitrary constants via symmetry action on a particular solution is reported. No subsequent work appears to settle it.

status_evidence.title: Progresses on Some Open Problems Related to Infinitely Many Symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems including arbitrary constants in special solutions via symmetry transformations.
status_evidence.claim: The question of introducing infinitely many arbitrary constants via the infinite symmetry algebra is identified as an open problem; partial progress and a conjecture are offered but no full resolution.

status_evidence.title: From one to infinity: symmetries of integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of symmetries of integrable systems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys discuss infinitely many symmetries without resolving whether an infinite sequence of arbitrary constants can be introduced into a particular solution.
